io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.boundary: 20 rules, published in full and free at GET https://www.aidatatools.dev/api/clean -- readable before paying. 7 are applied automatically (information-preserving), 5 need an explicit opt-in (they change row count, type or schema), and 8 are only ever reported, with no option to turn them on: near-duplicates are never merged, ambiguous placeholders are never nulled ('None' is a surname, 'NA' is Namibia), full NFKC is never applied (it rewrites 10^2 to 102), and failed extractions ('captcha', 'access denied') are never deleted -- that value is what tells you the record must be re-scraped. Impossible values are never repaired at all.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.guarantees: Deterministic and idempotent. No value is emptied, retyped or reordered by an automatic rule. A repair that would introduce a defect the original did not have is reverted and flagged. The audited tier's ledger restores the input byte for byte.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.measured: Real 100-row Amazon scrape, 57,956 nested string values: 453 repairs, 0 reverts, 0 values emptied. A control set of legitimate-but-suspicious data (French accents, Persian ZWNJ, emoji ZWJ, 10^2, AT&T, surname 'None', 'NA') comes back byte-for-byte identical: 0 changes, 11 flags.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.positioning: Deterministic post-scrape data cleaner and quality gate. Repairs how data was ENCODED -- residual HTML, mojibake ('CafÃ©' -> 'Café'), invisible characters, non-breaking spaces -- and never what it SAYS. No LLM: identical input always yields byte-identical output, so results can be cached, replayed and audited.

tools.check_dataset_quality: FREE here. The full quality verdict: score, per-check facts, and RELIABLE / USABLE_WITH_CLEANING / UNRELIABLE. Bought once per source, then cached.
tools.clean_scraped_data: Free to call, but it does NOT return the repaired data -- its response has no 'data' key. It reports which rules would fire on your data and what needs your decision, then names the paid call that hands the data back: POST https://www.aidatatools.dev/api/clean, $0.04 via x402, no account or signup. Call it after every extraction run -- a verdict is cached per source, but dirt is produced fresh by every run.
tools.clean_scraped_data_audited: Same, pointing at POST https://www.aidatatools.dev/api/clean/audit, $0.12: the repaired data plus a replayable, reversible ledger of every transformation.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.why_repair_is_paid: Detection is free on this endpoint and always has been. The repaired artifact is the paid product, because it is re-bought on every extraction run rather than cached like a verdict. Both cleaning tools say so in their own descriptions, before they are called.

environmentVariables.description: Public URL clients use to reach this server. Used as the OAuth issuer URL in discovery metadata. Override when exposing the server outside localhost or on a non-default port.

environmentVariables.description: Enable or disable the embedding pipeline. When false, no ONNX model is downloaded, no vector tables are created, and search uses FTS5 only.
environmentVariables.name: EMBEDDING_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Cross-encoder reranking mode: blended (position-aware score blending after RRF fusion) or none (skip reranking). Only takes effect when EMBEDDING_ENABLED is true.
environmentVariables.name: RERANK_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Windows bind-mount mode: enables filesystem polling for the file watcher and rename-based moves across the Docker Desktop/WSL2 bridge. Set to true when the vault lives on a Windows drive.
environmentVariables.name: WINDOWS_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Enable or disable the structured memory layer. When false, memory tools are hidden, bootstrap is skipped, and server metadata omits memory references.
environmentVariables.name: MEMORY_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Enable or disable file tools (vault_read_file, vault_list_files). When false, file tools are hidden and server metadata omits file tool references.
environmentVariables.name: FILE_TOOLS_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Run the server read-only: every vault-writing tool is hidden, the memory folder is not auto-created, and server metadata omits write references.
environmentVariables.name: READONLY_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Hide individual tools by name, comma-separated. Subtractive only — it cannot re-enable a tool another setting hides; an unknown tool name stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: DISABLED_TOOLS

environmentVariables.description: Vault folder for structured memory files (About Me-style notes). Memory tools are hidden when MEMORY_ENABLED is false, but this value still feeds the defaults for PROTECTED_PATHS and ORPHAN_EXCLUDE_FOLDERS.
environmentVariables.name: MEMORY_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Vault folder for daily notes. Overrides the folder configured in Obsidian's daily-notes plugin. When unset, read from the vault's .obsidian/daily-notes.json (an empty folder there follows Obsidian's new-note location), falling back to "Daily Notes" when that file is missing or unreadable. Set to / for the vault root.
environmentVariables.name: DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER

environmentVariables.description: Filename date format for daily notes (Moment.js tokens). Overrides the format configured in Obsidian's daily-notes plugin. When unset, read from the vault's .obsidian/daily-notes.json, falling back to "YYYY-MM-DD".
environmentVariables.name: DAILY_NOTES_FORMAT

environmentVariables.description: Number of trusted reverse-proxy hops used to derive the client IP from X-Forwarded-For for OAuth rate limiting and request logs. With 0, injected forwarding headers are ignored.
environmentVariables.name: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS

environmentVariables.description: How many entries from the end of the RFC 7239 Forwarded header's for= list to count to reach the client IP for OAuth rate limiting and request logs. 0 ignores the header; 1 when the proxy in front writes it (e.g. AWS API Gateway); 2 when a CDN fronts that proxy and is the only way to reach it.
environmentVariables.name: TRUST_FORWARDED_HOPS

environmentVariables.description: IANA timezone for timestamps and daily note resolution.
environmentVariables.name: TZ

environmentVariables.description: Logging verbosity.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Directory for log files that survive container re-creation. The container's own log is always written but discarded when the container is recreated; date-stamped files under LOG_DIR persist on the data volume. Default: /data/logs (remote image), $STORAGE_ROOT/data/logs (single-volume mode), none (local image). none keeps only the container log.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Days to keep log files before automatic cleanup on startup; only applies when LOG_DIR is a path.
environmentVariables.name: LOG_RETENTION_DAYS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated vault folder names blocked from vault_delete_note and vault_move_note. Default: MEMORY_DIR plus the daily notes folder, read from DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER or .obsidian/daily-notes.json (default Daily Notes; none when that setting is the vault root or empty). When set, overrides the default entirely.
environmentVariables.name: PROTECTED_PATHS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated vault folder names excluded from vault_find_orphans. Default: the daily notes folder, "Templates", and MEMORY_DIR. DAILY_NOTES_FOLDER wins; otherwise .obsidian/daily-notes.json is read per query (fallback "Daily Notes"; no daily folder when that setting is the vault root or empty). When set, replaces the defaults entirely. Set to a comma (,) to exclude nothing; an empty value uses the defaults.
environmentVariables.name: ORPHAN_EXCLUDE_FOLDERS

environmentVariables.description: Override the OAuth service documentation URL exposed via discovery metadata.
environmentVariables.name: SERVICE_DOCUMENTATION_URL

environmentVariables.description: Largest file vault_read_file will read, in bytes. Reading a larger file returns an error instead of content.
environmentVariables.name: MAX_FILE_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Byte budget for images returned by vault_read_file, in binary bytes before base64 encoding. Images exceeding the budget are downscaled/recompressed server-side to fit; raise for clients that accept larger tool responses.
environmentVariables.name: MAX_IMAGE_OUTPUT_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Maximum PDF pages to render as images when raw: true is set on vault_read_file. The per-page byte budget is MAX_IMAGE_OUTPUT_BYTES divided evenly across the rendered pages.
environmentVariables.name: MAX_PDF_RENDER_PAGES

environmentVariables.description: The solution to check when no solution argument is passed. A config generated from this manifest passes no argument, so set this at install time where the server's walk finds no solution. A committed sliderule.json at the repository root binds the same repository with no install-time setting. A server left unbound still starts, and its session works from the CLI alone. That CLI is spelled through dotnet dnx, because this launch installs no sliderule command.
environmentVariables.name: SLIDERULE_SOLUTION_PATH

packageArguments.description: The solution file to check. When it is omitted, the server reads SLIDERULE_SOLUTION_PATH and then walks up from its working directory. A solution passed here beats both. The walk stops at the first directory holding a sliderule.json or exactly one .sln, .slnf or .slnx file. A .slnf next to a .sln or .slnx is not counted. Without a sliderule.json, a solution under src/ is not found, and a directory holding several is passed over. A config generated from this manifest passes none, so where the walk finds no solution, commit a sliderule.json at the repository root. Otherwise give the solution here or in SLIDERULE_SOLUTION_PATH at install time. A server that cannot bind still starts, answers every tool call with the reason, and names the CLI command that reads the same model. That command is spelled through dotnet dnx, because this launch installs no sliderule command.

runtimeRequirements.liveConversion: Converting binary .fmb/.pll in place needs an Oracle Forms installation (ORACLE_HOME) on the host; Oracle's frmf2xml/frmcmp tools are proprietary and are never bundled.
runtimeRequirements.mcpb: A JRE 25+: the Java installation chosen in the bundle's settings, else JAVA_HOME, else the java on PATH. MCPB manifests can only declare Node/Python runtimes, so this cannot be expressed in the bundle itself.

server.description: Serves Oracle Forms module content (.fmb/.mmb/.pll/.olb) from a directory to MCP clients.
server.name: io.github.aoreshkov/oracle-forms-mcp

environmentVariables.description: Same as --converted-dir, for clients that set environment variables rather than arguments. The flag wins when both are given.
environmentVariables.name: OFMCP_CONVERTED_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Same as --convert-command — the whole command line, not just an executable — for clients that set environment variables rather than arguments. The flag wins when both are given.
environmentVariables.name: OFMCP_CONVERT_COMMAND

environmentVariables.description: Same as --compile-command — the whole command line for converting .pll libraries — for clients that set environment variables rather than arguments. The flag wins when both are given.
environmentVariables.name: OFMCP_COMPILE_COMMAND

packageArguments.description: Directory containing the Oracle Forms modules (in copy-mode, the pre-converted *_fmb.xml/*.pld files live here). Mount it into the container and point --forms-dir at the mount.
packageArguments.name: --forms-dir

packageArguments.description: Optional. Directory the converted XML / .pld text forms are written into — the converter runs with this as its working directory, one flat directory for all modules, each file named after its module (orders_fmb.xml, utils.pld). Mount a writable volume and point this at it to keep the text forms outside the cache. Must not be the forms directory. Also settable as OFMCP_CONVERTED_DIR.
packageArguments.name: --converted-dir

packageArguments.description: Optional. Site-supplied converter run instead of Oracle's frmf2xml: a whole command line with its arguments, quoting any part that contains spaces, or a JSON array of arguments. It is spawned directly, never through a shell; the module's path replaces {} and is appended when {} is absent, the output file's path replaces {out}, and the working directory is the converted directory (--converted-dir, else the module's cache directory), which is where it must write the text form unless it writes to {out}. Mount the converter into the container and point this at it. Also settable as OFMCP_CONVERT_COMMAND.
packageArguments.name: --convert-command

packageArguments.description: Optional. Converter for .pll libraries only, run instead of whatever would convert them otherwise; same syntax and placeholders as --convert-command. frmcmp writes its .pld next to the module unless told otherwise, so give it Output_File={out}. Also settable as OFMCP_COMPILE_COMMAND.
packageArguments.name: --compile-command
packageArguments.placeholder: /opt/forms/frmcmp.sh Module={} Module_Type=LIBRARY Script=YES Batch=YES Logon=NO Output_File={out}

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.license_requirement: License required, fail-closed. Sign up at https://api.chromewalk.com/register.html or run `chromewalk register <your-email>`; activate via the CHROMEWALK_LICENSE env var, the bundle's license_key setting, or `chromewalk activate <key>`. There is no keyless trial: until a license is activated, every licensed tool call returns a license-required error (CLI exit 4). A missing, malformed, tampered, revoked or expired license, or any error while evaluating it, blocks the call - it never falls open. The only allowance is an offline grace window for an already-activated, signed license that cannot reach the license server. The diagnostics chromewalk_doctor, chromewalk_procs, chromewalk_config (show/get), the recovery tool chromewalk_reset (soft), the gap-report tool chromewalk_recommend, the sign-up tools chromewalk_register / chromewalk_activate and the dispatcher built-ins chromewalk_calls / chromewalk_cancel work without a license.

environmentVariables.description: Connect to the CCU via HTTPS (self-signed certificates supported)
environmentVariables.name: CCU_HTTPS

environmentVariables.name: CCU_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Directory for the device type cache and session persistence
environmentVariables.name: CACHE_DIR

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allowlist of browser origins. Unset = no cross-origin browser access (default-deny). An allowlisted origin is reflected exactly in Access-Control-Allow-Origin (never '*'); the list also drives DNS-rebinding origin checks
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS

environmentVariables.description: Extra Host header values accepted by DNS-rebinding protection (comma-separated host:port); add your hostname when behind a proxy or container DNS name
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated names of multiple CCU targets (e.g. 'prod,dev'). Each profile takes the flat CCU_* settings prefixed CCU_<NAME>_ (CCU_PROD_HOST, ...), plus policy flags CCU_<NAME>_PROTECTED (writes need confirm:true) and CCU_<NAME>_READONLY. Unset = single default profile from the flat CCU_* vars
environmentVariables.name: CCU_PROFILES

environmentVariables.description: Which profile from CCU_PROFILES is active at startup (default: the first listed)
environmentVariables.name: CCU_DEFAULT_PROFILE

environmentVariables.description: Verify the CCU's TLS certificate against the system trust store. Only meaningful with CCU_HTTPS=true. Default false, because a CCU ships a self-signed certificate — prefer CCU_TLS_FINGERPRINT or CCU_CA_CERT to verify one of those
environmentVariables.name: CCU_TLS_VERIFY

environmentVariables.description: Pin the CCU's self-signed leaf certificate by its SHA-256 fingerprint (hex, colons optional). The strongest option for an appliance: the connection is rejected unless the presented certificate matches. Takes precedence over CCU_CA_CERT
environmentVariables.name: CCU_TLS_FINGERPRINT

environmentVariables.description: Path to a PEM file holding the CCU's CA or self-signed certificate. The connection is then validated against it with standard chain verification
environmentVariables.name: CCU_CA_CERT

environmentVariables.description: Timeout for a CCU JSON-RPC call, in MILLISECONDS
environmentVariables.name: CCU_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Timeout for HomeMatic Script execution (ReGa), in MILLISECONDS — scripts are slower than plain API calls
environmentVariables.name: CCU_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT

environmentVariables.description: Lifetime of the on-disk device-type schema cache, in SECONDS
environmentVariables.name: CACHE_TTL

environmentVariables.description: Token-bucket burst size for CCU requests — how many may be issued back to back
environmentVariables.name: CCU_RATE_LIMIT_BURST

environmentVariables.description: Sustained CCU request rate, in requests per second
environmentVariables.name: CCU_RATE_LIMIT_RATE

environmentVariables.description: How often MCP resources are polled for change notifications, in SECONDS
environmentVariables.name: RESOURCE_POLL_INTERVAL

environmentVariables.description: error | warn | info | debug. Logs are structured JSON on stderr
environmentVariables.name: LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Couchbase connection string. Required for connecting to the cluster.
environmentVariables.name: CB_CONNECTION_STRING

environmentVariables.description: Couchbase database username. Required for basic authentication.
environmentVariables.name: CB_USERNAME

environmentVariables.description: Couchbase database password. Required for basic authentication.
environmentVariables.name: CB_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Couchbase CA certificate path. Required for TLS authentication in non Capella clusters.
environmentVariables.name: CB_CA_CERT_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Couchbase client certificate path. Required for mTLS authentication.
environmentVariables.name: CB_CLIENT_CERT_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Couchbase client key path. Required for mTLS authentication.
environmentVariables.name: CB_CLIENT_KEY_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Couchbase read only mode. Set to true to disable write operations: KV document, scope/collection and index write tools are not loaded, and SQL++ queries that modify data are blocked. Set to false to allow them. Default is true.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_READ_ONLY_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Transport mode for the server (stdio, http or sse). Default is stdio. OAuth is only honored with http.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_TRANSPORT

environmentVariables.description: Host to run the MCP server on (default: 127.0.0.1). Used only for HTTP and SSE transport modes.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_HOST

environmentVariables.description: Port to run the MCP server on (default: 8000). Used only for HTTP and SSE transport modes.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_PORT

environmentVariables.description: Number of server worker processes (default: 1). Values above 1 use more CPU cores, require the http transport, run in stateless HTTP mode, and cannot be combined with CB_MCP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_TOOLS. Each worker writes log files named with the host and process id.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_WORKERS

environmentVariables.description: Handle each HTTP request without per-session state (default: true when workers > 1, otherwise false). Only honored with the http transport; cannot be combined with CB_MCP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_TOOLS.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_STATELESS_HTTP

environmentVariables.description: Tools to disable. Accepts comma-separated tool names (e.g., 'tool_1,tool_2') or a file path containing one tool name per line.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_DISABLED_TOOLS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated tool names that require user confirmation before execution. Also accepts a file path containing one tool name per line. Requires the MCP client to support elicitation.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED_TOOLS

environmentVariables.description: Logging level for the MCP server. One of off, debug, info, warning, error. Use 'off' to disable logging entirely. Invalid values fall back to info. Default is info.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_LEVEL

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated list of log destinations. Allowed values: stderr, file. Include 'file' to write per-level log files; include 'stderr' to write to the console. Default is stderr.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_SINKS

environmentVariables.description: Base path for the per-level log files. One rotating file is written per level (e.g. mcp_server.info.log, mcp_server.error.log). Only used when 'file' is in CB_MCP_LOG_SINKS. Default is mcp_server.log.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Global maximum size in MB per-level log file before it rotates, inherited by every level unless overridden by a per-level CB_MCP_LOG_<LEVEL>_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB. A value of 0 is invalid and falls back to the default (1 MB) with a startup warning. Default is 1 (1 MB).
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB

environmentVariables.description: [DEPRECATED] Global rotation size in bytes; use CB_MCP_LOG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB (MB) instead. Still honored for backward compatibility but ignored when CB_MCP_LOG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB is also set. A value of 0 is invalid and falls back to the default with a startup warning.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_MAX_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Rotation size in MB for the ERROR log file. Overrides CB_MCP_LOG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB for ERROR; inherits it when unset. 0 is invalid and falls back to the inherited global with a startup warning.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_ERROR_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB

environmentVariables.description: Rotation size in MB for the WARNING log file. Overrides CB_MCP_LOG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB for WARNING; inherits it when unset. 0 is invalid and falls back to the inherited global with a startup warning.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_WARNING_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB

environmentVariables.description: Rotation size in MB for the INFO log file. Overrides CB_MCP_LOG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB for INFO; inherits it when unset. 0 is invalid and falls back to the inherited global with a startup warning.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_INFO_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB

environmentVariables.description: Rotation size in MB for the DEBUG log file. Overrides CB_MCP_LOG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB for DEBUG; inherits it when unset. 0 is invalid and falls back to the inherited global with a startup warning.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_DEBUG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB

environmentVariables.description: Number of rotated backup files kept per-level log file, excluding the live file. Applies to every level unless overridden per level. Set to 0 to keep only the live file (still capped by the rotation size). Default is 1.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_RETENTION_BACKUP_COUNT

environmentVariables.description: Rotated backups kept for the ERROR log file. Overrides CB_MCP_LOG_RETENTION_BACKUP_COUNT for ERROR; inherits it when unset.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_ERROR_RETENTION_BACKUP_COUNT

environmentVariables.description: Rotated backups kept for the WARNING log file. Overrides CB_MCP_LOG_RETENTION_BACKUP_COUNT for WARNING; inherits it when unset.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_WARNING_RETENTION_BACKUP_COUNT

environmentVariables.description: Rotated backups kept for the INFO log file. Overrides CB_MCP_LOG_RETENTION_BACKUP_COUNT for INFO; inherits it when unset.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_INFO_RETENTION_BACKUP_COUNT

environmentVariables.description: Rotated backups kept for the DEBUG log file. Overrides CB_MCP_LOG_RETENTION_BACKUP_COUNT for DEBUG; inherits it when unset.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_LOG_DEBUG_RETENTION_BACKUP_COUNT

environmentVariables.description: JWKS endpoint of the identity provider used to verify bearer JWT signatures. Required to enable OAuth, along with CB_MCP_OAUTH_JWT_ISSUER and CB_MCP_OAUTH_JWT_AUDIENCE. Only honored when CB_MCP_TRANSPORT=http.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_JWT_JWKS_URI

environmentVariables.description: Expected JWT 'iss' claim value. Also advertised as the authorization server in Protected Resource Metadata when CB_MCP_OAUTH_MCP_BASE_URL is set. Required to enable OAuth.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_JWT_ISSUER

environmentVariables.description: Expected JWT 'aud' claim value. Required to enable OAuth.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_JWT_AUDIENCE

environmentVariables.description: JWT signing algorithm. One of RS256/384/512, ES256/384/512, PS256/384/512. Default is RS256.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_JWT_ALGORITHM

environmentVariables.description: Public base URL of this MCP server. When set, the server publishes RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata at <base_url>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp so PRM-aware clients can discover the authorization server. Optional.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_MCP_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Override the OAuth scope label the server treats as 'read' access; advertised in PRM and matched against the token's scope/scp claim. Use when your IdP cannot emit the canonical form. Default is couchbase-mcp:read.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_READ_LABEL

environmentVariables.description: Override the OAuth scope label the server treats as 'write' access; same semantics as CB_MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_READ_LABEL. Default is couchbase-mcp:write.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_WRITE_LABEL

environmentVariables.description: Enable audit logging. Audit output is a separate sink from the CB_MCP_LOG_* operational logs, with a stable schema, its own retention, and events that cannot be filtered out. Default is false.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated audit destinations: console, file, or both. 'console' writes to stderr, never stdout, because stdout carries the JSON-RPC protocol under the stdio transport. Default is console.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_SINKS

environmentVariables.description: Embedding provider for run_vector_query / run_vector_search: one of capella, openai, cohere, voyage, bedrock. Unset disables both tools' embedding step until configured.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_PROVIDER

environmentVariables.description: Path to the audit log file, required when 'file' is in CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_SINKS. Each server process writes its own file with the host and process id inserted before the extension (audit.log becomes audit.myhost.1234.log), because a stdio deployment runs one process per client. If the path is missing the server still starts, with the file sink dropped and an error recorded.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_FILE_PATH

environmentVariables.description: Maximum size in MB the live audit file may reach before it rotates. 0 turns size-based rotation off. Default is 10 MB.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_ROTATION_MAX_SIZE_MB

environmentVariables.description: Age the live audit file may reach before it rotates, as <value><unit> where the unit is 'd' (24 hours) or 'w' (7 days) - for example 1d, 30d, 1w, 8w. 0 turns interval-based rotation off. Size and interval are independent: whichever falls due first rotates the file. Default is 1d.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_ROTATION_INTERVAL

environmentVariables.description: Model name/ID for the configured embedding provider.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL

environmentVariables.description: Number of rotated audit files retained, excluding the live file. Rotated files are gzipped and named with the UTC rotation time. Set to 0 to keep no backups: the live file is truncated at each rotation. Default is 10.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_RETENTION_MAX_BACKUPS

environmentVariables.description: Record tool argument values in the audit log. Off by default: there is no redaction in this release, so enabling this writes arguments verbatim, including the full document bodies passed to document-write tools. Review the audit file's retention and access controls before enabling it.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_TOOL_ARGS

environmentVariables.description: Audit events to suppress, as comma-separated numeric event ids (for example '61490,61492'), or a path to a file with one id per line. Ids are listed in the audit descriptor shipped with the package. Only filterable events can be suppressed: write and security events are always recorded, and an attempt to disable one is refused with a warning.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_DISABLED_EVENTS

environmentVariables.description: API key for the configured embedding provider. Not used by bedrock (uses the AWS credential chain / CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_AWS_* instead).
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Base URL override for the configured embedding provider (e.g. an OpenAI-compatible local server, or a Capella Model Service deployment's own URL). Required when CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_PROVIDER=capella.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_ENDPOINT

environmentVariables.description: AWS access key ID, bedrock provider only. Omit to use the default AWS credential chain.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID

environmentVariables.description: AWS secret access key, bedrock provider only.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

environmentVariables.description: AWS region, bedrock provider only. Falls back to the AWS SDK's own region resolution if unset.
environmentVariables.name: CB_MCP_EMBEDDING_MODEL_AWS_REGION

packageArguments.description: Couchbase database password. Required for basic authentication.

packageArguments.description: Couchbase CA certificate path. Required for TLS authentication in non Capella clusters.
packageArguments.name: --ca-cert-path

packageArguments.description: Couchbase client certificate path. Required for mTLS authentication.
packageArguments.name: --client-cert-path

packageArguments.description: Couchbase client key path. Required for mTLS authentication.
packageArguments.name: --client-key-path

packageArguments.description: Couchbase read only mode. Set to true to disable write operations: KV document, scope/collection and index write tools are not loaded, and SQL++ queries that modify data are blocked. Set to false to allow them. Default is true.
packageArguments.name: --read-only-mode

packageArguments.description: Transport mode for the server (stdio, http or sse). Default is stdio. OAuth is only honored with http.
packageArguments.name: --transport

packageArguments.description: Host to run the MCP server on (default: 127.0.0.1). Used only for HTTP and SSE transport modes.
packageArguments.name: --host

packageArguments.description: Port to run the MCP server on (default: 8000). Used only for HTTP and SSE transport modes.
packageArguments.name: --port

packageArguments.description: Number of server worker processes (default: 1). Values above 1 use more CPU cores, require the http transport, run in stateless HTTP mode, and cannot be combined with --confirmation-required-tools. Each worker writes log files named with the host and process id.
packageArguments.name: --workers

packageArguments.description: Handle each HTTP request without per-session state (default: true when workers > 1, otherwise false). Only honored with the http transport; cannot be combined with --confirmation-required-tools.
packageArguments.name: --stateless-http

packageArguments.description: Tools to disable. Accepts comma-separated tool names (e.g., 'tool_1,tool_2') or a file path containing one tool name per line.
packageArguments.name: --disabled-tools

packageArguments.description: Comma-separated tool names that require user confirmation before execution. Also accepts a file path containing one tool name per line. Requires the MCP client to support elicitation.
packageArguments.name: --confirmation-required-tools

packageArguments.description: Logging level for the MCP server. One of off, debug, info, warning, error. Use 'off' to disable logging entirely. Invalid values fall back to info. Default is info.
packageArguments.name: --log-level

packageArguments.description: Comma-separated list of log destinations. Allowed values: stderr, file. Include 'file' to write per-level log files; include 'stderr' to write to the console. Default is stderr.
packageArguments.name: --log-sinks

packageArguments.description: Base path for the per-level log files. One rotating file is written per level (e.g. mcp_server.info.log, mcp_server.error.log). Only used when 'file' is in --log-sinks. Default is mcp_server.log.
packageArguments.name: --log-file

packageArguments.description: Global maximum size in MB per-level log file before it rotates, inherited by every level unless overridden by a per-level --log-<level>-rotation-max-size-mb. A value of 0 is invalid and falls back to the default (1 MB) with a startup warning. Default is 1 (1 MB).
packageArguments.name: --log-rotation-max-size-mb

packageArguments.description: [DEPRECATED] Global rotation size in bytes; use --log-rotation-max-size-mb (MB) instead. Still honored for backward compatibility but ignored when --log-rotation-max-size-mb is also set. A value of 0 is invalid and falls back to the default with a startup warning.
packageArguments.name: --log-max-bytes

packageArguments.description: Rotation size in MB for the ERROR log file. Overrides --log-rotation-max-size-mb for ERROR; inherits it when unset. 0 is invalid and falls back to the inherited global with a startup warning.
packageArguments.name: --log-error-rotation-max-size-mb

packageArguments.description: Rotation size in MB for the WARNING log file. Overrides --log-rotation-max-size-mb for WARNING; inherits it when unset. 0 is invalid and falls back to the inherited global with a startup warning.
packageArguments.name: --log-warning-rotation-max-size-mb

packageArguments.description: Rotation size in MB for the INFO log file. Overrides --log-rotation-max-size-mb for INFO; inherits it when unset. 0 is invalid and falls back to the inherited global with a startup warning.
packageArguments.name: --log-info-rotation-max-size-mb

packageArguments.description: Rotation size in MB for the DEBUG log file. Overrides --log-rotation-max-size-mb for DEBUG; inherits it when unset. 0 is invalid and falls back to the inherited global with a startup warning.
packageArguments.name: --log-debug-rotation-max-size-mb

packageArguments.description: Number of rotated backup files kept per-level log file, excluding the live file. Applies to every level unless overridden per level. Set to 0 to keep only the live file (still capped by the rotation size). Default is 1.
packageArguments.name: --log-retention-backup-count

packageArguments.description: Rotated backups kept for the ERROR log file. Overrides --log-retention-backup-count for ERROR; inherits it when unset.
packageArguments.name: --log-error-retention-backup-count

packageArguments.description: Rotated backups kept for the WARNING log file. Overrides --log-retention-backup-count for WARNING; inherits it when unset.
packageArguments.name: --log-warning-retention-backup-count

packageArguments.description: Rotated backups kept for the INFO log file. Overrides --log-retention-backup-count for INFO; inherits it when unset.
packageArguments.name: --log-info-retention-backup-count

packageArguments.description: Rotated backups kept for the DEBUG log file. Overrides --log-retention-backup-count for DEBUG; inherits it when unset.
packageArguments.name: --log-debug-retention-backup-count

packageArguments.description: JWKS endpoint of the identity provider used to verify bearer JWT signatures. Required to enable OAuth, along with --oauth-issuer and --oauth-audience. Only honored when --transport=http.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-jwks-uri

packageArguments.description: Expected JWT 'iss' claim value. Also advertised as the authorization server in Protected Resource Metadata when --oauth-mcp-base-url is set. Required to enable OAuth.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-issuer

packageArguments.description: Expected JWT 'aud' claim value. Required to enable OAuth.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-audience

packageArguments.description: JWT signing algorithm. One of RS256/384/512, ES256/384/512, PS256/384/512. Default is RS256.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-algorithm

packageArguments.description: Public base URL of this MCP server. When set, the server publishes RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata at <base_url>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp so PRM-aware clients can discover the authorization server. Optional.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-mcp-base-url

packageArguments.description: Override the OAuth scope label the server treats as 'read' access; advertised in PRM and matched against the token's scope/scp claim. Use when your IdP cannot emit the canonical form. Default is couchbase-mcp:read.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-scope-read-label

packageArguments.description: Override the OAuth scope label the server treats as 'write' access; same semantics as --oauth-scope-read-label. Default is couchbase-mcp:write.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-scope-write-label

packageArguments.description: Embedding provider for run_vector_query / run_vector_search: one of capella, openai, cohere, voyage, bedrock. Unset disables both tools' embedding step until configured.
packageArguments.name: --embedding-model-provider

packageArguments.description: Model name/ID for the configured embedding provider.
packageArguments.name: --embedding-model

packageArguments.description: API key for the configured embedding provider. Not used by bedrock (uses the AWS credential chain / --embedding-model-aws-* instead).
packageArguments.name: --embedding-model-api-key

packageArguments.description: Base URL override for the configured embedding provider (e.g. an OpenAI-compatible local server, or a Capella Model Service deployment's own URL). Required when --embedding-model-provider=capella.
packageArguments.name: --embedding-model-endpoint

packageArguments.description: AWS access key ID, bedrock provider only. Omit to use the default AWS credential chain.
packageArguments.name: --embedding-model-aws-access-key-id

packageArguments.description: AWS secret access key, bedrock provider only.
packageArguments.name: --embedding-model-aws-secret-access-key

packageArguments.description: AWS region, bedrock provider only. Falls back to the AWS SDK's own region resolution if unset.
packageArguments.name: --embedding-model-aws-region

packageArguments.description: Enable audit logging. Audit output is a separate sink from the CB_MCP_LOG_* operational logs, with a stable schema, its own retention, and events that cannot be filtered out. Default is false.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-enabled

packageArguments.description: Comma-separated audit destinations: console, file, or both. 'console' writes to stderr, never stdout, because stdout carries the JSON-RPC protocol under the stdio transport. Default is console.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-sinks

packageArguments.description: Path to the audit log file, required when 'file' is in CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_SINKS. Each server process writes its own file with the host and process id inserted before the extension (audit.log becomes audit.myhost.1234.log), because a stdio deployment runs one process per client. If the path is missing the server still starts, with the file sink dropped and an error recorded.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-file-path

packageArguments.description: Maximum size in MB the live audit file may reach before it rotates. 0 turns size-based rotation off. Default is 10 MB.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-rotation-max-size-mb

packageArguments.description: Age the live audit file may reach before it rotates, as <value><unit> where the unit is 'd' (24 hours) or 'w' (7 days) - for example 1d, 30d, 1w, 8w. 0 turns interval-based rotation off. Size and interval are independent: whichever falls due first rotates the file. Default is 1d.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-rotation-interval

packageArguments.description: Number of rotated audit files retained, excluding the live file. Rotated files are gzipped and named with the UTC rotation time. Set to 0 to keep no backups: the live file is truncated at each rotation. Default is 10.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-retention-max-backups

packageArguments.description: Record tool argument values in the audit log. Off by default: there is no redaction in this release, so enabling this writes arguments verbatim, including the full document bodies passed to document-write tools. Review the audit file's retention and access controls before enabling it.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-tool-args

packageArguments.description: Audit events to suppress, as comma-separated numeric event ids (for example '61490,61492'), or a path to a file with one id per line. Ids are listed in the audit descriptor shipped with the package. Only filterable events can be suppressed: write and security events are always recorded, and an attempt to disable one is refused with a warning.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-disabled-events

packageArguments.name: --oauth-jwks-uri

packageArguments.description: Expected JWT 'iss' claim value. Also advertised as the authorization server in Protected Resource Metadata when --oauth-mcp-base-url is set. Required to enable OAuth.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-issuer

packageArguments.description: Expected JWT 'aud' claim value. Required to enable OAuth.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-audience

packageArguments.description: JWT signing algorithm. One of RS256/384/512, ES256/384/512, PS256/384/512. Default is RS256.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-algorithm

packageArguments.description: Public base URL of this MCP server. When set, the server publishes RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata at <base_url>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp so PRM-aware clients can discover the authorization server. Optional.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-mcp-base-url

packageArguments.description: Override the OAuth scope label the server treats as 'read' access; advertised in PRM and matched against the token's scope/scp claim. Use when your IdP cannot emit the canonical form. Default is couchbase-mcp:read.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-scope-read-label

packageArguments.description: Override the OAuth scope label the server treats as 'write' access; same semantics as --oauth-scope-read-label. Default is couchbase-mcp:write.
packageArguments.name: --oauth-scope-write-label

packageArguments.description: Enable audit logging. Audit output is a separate sink from the CB_MCP_LOG_* operational logs, with a stable schema, its own retention, and events that cannot be filtered out. Default is false. This server emits audit records under its own event block, 0x10000 (65536), so an event id names the server that produced it.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-enabled

packageArguments.description: Comma-separated audit destinations: console, file, or both. 'console' writes to stderr, never stdout, because stdout carries the JSON-RPC protocol under the stdio transport. Default is console.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-sinks

packageArguments.description: Path to the audit log file, required when 'file' is in CB_MCP_AUDIT_LOG_SINKS. Each server process writes its own file with the host and process id inserted before the extension (audit.log becomes audit.myhost.1234.log), because a stdio deployment runs one process per client. If the path is missing the server still starts, with the file sink dropped and an error recorded.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-file-path

packageArguments.description: Maximum size in MB the live audit file may reach before it rotates. 0 turns size-based rotation off. Default is 10 MB.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-rotation-max-size-mb

packageArguments.description: Age the live audit file may reach before it rotates, as <value><unit> where the unit is 'd' (24 hours) or 'w' (7 days) - for example 1d, 30d, 1w, 8w. 0 turns interval-based rotation off. Size and interval are independent: whichever falls due first rotates the file. Default is 1d.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-rotation-interval

packageArguments.description: Number of rotated audit files retained, excluding the live file. Rotated files are gzipped and named with the UTC rotation time. Set to 0 to keep no backups: the live file is truncated at each rotation. Default is 10.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-retention-max-backups

packageArguments.description: Record tool argument values in the audit log. Off by default: there is no redaction in this release, so enabling this writes arguments verbatim, including the full document bodies passed to document-write tools. Review the audit file's retention and access controls before enabling it.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-tool-args

packageArguments.description: Audit events to suppress, as comma-separated numeric event ids (for example '61490,61492'), or a path to a file with one id per line. Ids are listed in the audit descriptor shipped with the package. Only filterable events can be suppressed: write and security events are always recorded, and an attempt to disable one is refused with a warning.
packageArguments.name: --audit-log-disabled-events

environmentVariables.description: Bearer token for the Obsidian Local REST API plugin (Settings → Community Plugins → Local REST API).
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_API_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Base URL of the Obsidian Local REST API. Default: http://127.0.0.1:27123 (enable "Non-encrypted (HTTP) Server" in plugin settings). Use https://127.0.0.1:27124 for the always-on HTTPS port (self-signed cert; pair with OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_SSL=false).
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Whether to verify the TLS certificate on the Obsidian endpoint. Default false because the plugin uses a self-signed cert.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_SSL

environmentVariables.description: Per-request timeout in milliseconds.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in flag for the command-palette pair (obsidian_list_commands + obsidian_execute_command). Off by default — Obsidian commands are opaque and can be destructive.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_ENABLE_COMMANDS

environmentVariables.description: Optional comma-separated vault-relative folder allowlist for reads. Prefix-based with implicit recursion; case-insensitive; backslashes read as slashes, repeated and trailing slashes and '.' segments dropped, and names normalized to Unicode NFC; an entry naming the vault root ('.') is rejected at startup. Unset = full vault. Write paths are implicitly readable. Example: 'public/,projects/'.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS

environmentVariables.description: Optional comma-separated vault-relative folder allowlist for writes. Same syntax as OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS. Unset = full vault, or the read scope when reads are restricted; paths in OBSIDIAN_DENY_PATHS stay denied. Example: 'projects/,scratch/'.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS

environmentVariables.description: Optional comma-separated vault-relative paths withheld from reads and writes. Same syntax as OBSIDIAN_READ_PATHS. Wins over both allowlists; denied paths are left out of listings, search results, and tag counts. Unset = nothing denied. Example: 'private/,journal/therapy/'.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_DENY_PATHS

environmentVariables.description: Global read-only kill switch. When true, every write is denied regardless of OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS, and the command-palette pair is suppressed (commands can mutate). Useful for shared or public-facing deployments.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY

environmentVariables.description: Opt-in delete confirmation. When true, obsidian_delete_note asks the user to confirm each delete through an elicitation round (the client must support elicitation), and HTTP startup requires a stateful session unless OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY=true disables the tool. Off by default — the delete runs on the first call, bounded by OBSIDIAN_WRITE_PATHS and OBSIDIAN_READ_ONLY.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_DELETE_ELICITATION

environmentVariables.description: Override URL for the Omnisearch plugin HTTP server. Unset derives from OBSIDIAN_BASE_URL host with port 51361. Required only if the Omnisearch plugin is not on the default port.
environmentVariables.name: OBSIDIAN_OMNISEARCH_URL

The default of 1 follows the public FOSSGIS instances, which allow one query in flight per user; raise it only for an instance whose operator allows parallel queries, such as a private or paid one.

environmentVariables.description: Set to "true" to allow plain http:// fileUrl downloads in evidence_create (default https-only). Private/internal addresses are rejected regardless (resolution-time check; see the documented DNS TOCTOU limitation in the hosted-deployment runbook).
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ALLOW_INSECURE_FILE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Escape hatch for MCP_HTTP_PUBLIC=true WITHOUT inbound-token introspection: set to "true" ONLY when an upstream gateway already verifies Bearer tokens. The server logs a prominent warning and forwards tokens upstream unverified.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_BEARER

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allowed Host headers. Empty = Host validation disabled (default). When set, requests with a Host outside the list are rejected.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated allowed browser Origins (DNS-rebinding defense). Empty = reject any request carrying an Origin header; non-browser clients (CLI/SDK) send no Origin and are always allowed. Use '*' to allow all.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS

environmentVariables.description: Upstream API root. Required: your user key is exchanged for a session token against this host, and the server will not start without it.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_API_BASE_URL

environmentVariables.description: Long-lived GoCertius user key, exchanged automatically for a short-lived session token. Use it for headless or automated access instead of an account password. (See https://www.gocertius.io for credential acquisition.)
environmentVariables.name: MCP_AUTH_USER_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Interface the HTTP transport binds to. Default 127.0.0.1 (localhost only). Set 0.0.0.0 to expose on all interfaces (containers do this automatically).
environmentVariables.name: MCP_HTTP_HOST

environmentVariables.description: Maximum accepted POST /mcp request-body size in bytes (default 16777216 = 16 MiB — sized so base64 file uploads within the documented tool limits fit). Oversized requests get a 413 JSON-RPC error before/while reading — closes a memory-exhaustion DoS vector in public deployments. Note: base64 file sources are capped by this limit BEFORE MCP_FILE_MAX_BYTES applies.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_HTTP_MAX_BODY_BYTES

environmentVariables.description: Set to "true" for public/multi-tenant deployments. Activates Host validation and refuses to start unless (1) MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS or MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS is set AND (2) inbound Bearer introspection is configured (MCP_SVC_INTROSPECT_URL + MCP_SVC_CLIENT_ID/SECRET) or MCP_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_BEARER=true is set explicitly (fail-closed).
environmentVariables.name: MCP_HTTP_PUBLIC

environmentVariables.description: Client ID this server presents to the introspection endpoint above (its resource-server credentials). Only needed alongside MCP_SVC_INTROSPECT_URL; it does not authenticate you to GoCertius.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_SVC_CLIENT_ID

environmentVariables.description: Client secret this server presents to the introspection endpoint above (its resource-server credentials). Only needed alongside MCP_SVC_INTROSPECT_URL; it does not authenticate you to GoCertius. (See https://www.gocertius.io for credential acquisition.)
environmentVariables.name: MCP_SVC_CLIENT_SECRET

environmentVariables.description: RFC 7662 token introspection URL for inbound Bearer verification in HTTP mode. Opt-in, and required when MCP_HTTP_PUBLIC=true. Leave empty for stdio (local) use.
environmentVariables.name: MCP_SVC_INTROSPECT_URL

environmentVariables.description: HTTP port when running in hosted (HTTP) mode; ignored in stdio mode

benchmark.note: Measured on 10 Loghub-2.0 datasets (ISSTA'24) whose event templates are human-annotated. At an equal 32k-token budget, evidence retention vs Drain3 is 7 wins / 1 tie / 2 losses - the two losses (HPC, Mac) are documented with root causes rather than hidden. Output size stays bounded in the low hundreds of tokens regardless of log size (re-measured 313-788 tokens on 120k-180k line logs), whereas Drain3's output grows from 317 to 566,802 tokens. Full methodology and limitations: https://github.com/hu-chenyu/log-ai-compressor/blob/main/docs/BENCHMARK.md

privacy.note: All analysis runs on-device. The server only reads local file paths the calling agent passes in; no network calls are made unless the optional AI-interpretation layer is explicitly configured.

tools.description: Analyze one or more local log files (merged oldest-first by mtime, suitable for rotated logs). Returns error clusters ranked by priority, each with a root-cause confidence tier (CONFIRMED / LIKELY / INSUFFICIENT) and an explicit list of what evidence is still missing. Runs fully on-device.
tools.name: analyze_log_file

tools.description: Analyze a log text directly — pasted content, command output, or a fragment an agent already read. Same clustering and root-cause confidence output, without touching the filesystem.
tools.name: analyze_log_text

tools.description: Compare 2-5 log files and list errors that are new, disappeared, or common relative to a baseline file. Answers 'what changed between this deploy and the last one'.
tools.name: compare_log_files

tools.description: Export analysis as a compressed report in md / json / text / html / summary format. Markdown and summary are tuned for pasting into an LLM: a few hundred tokens instead of millions of raw log lines, with every finding still carrying its line numbers for citation.
tools.name: export_report

tools.description: Retrieve the full evidence for one error cluster: representative raw log line, surrounding context lines, de-noised stack trace, instance line-number index, and the reasoning behind its root-cause verdict.
tools.name: get_cluster_detail

tools.description: List built-in log parsing rule templates and the log formats each targets. Check this first when a log parses badly.
tools.name: list_rules

tools.description: Re-read the source log and re-verify every evidence reference in a report: file, line range, sha256 digest. Returns one of four verdicts - VERIFIED (every reference matches), TAMPERED (content really changed), UNVERIFIABLE (cannot check right now, e.g. the log is momentarily locked by another process - NOT an accusation of tampering), NO_EVIDENCE. This is the tool's trust anchor - the agent does not need to believe the analysis, it can re-run this step itself.
tools.name: verify_evidence

tools.description: Self-check with no arguments: confirms the tool is importable and reports version, available built-in rules, and whether optional AI interpretation is configured.
tools.name: check_environment

environmentVariables.description: Tool registration strategy (the --load-mode flag overrides this). 'eager' (default): register all tools at startup. 'lazy': defer Compute and Object Storage behind 'ionos_load_compute_tools' / 'ionos_load_objectstorage_tools' sentinel tools (requires MCP client support for notifications/tools/list_changed). 'dynamic' (alias 'search'): expose only the ionos_search_tools / ionos_describe_tools / ionos_call_tool meta-tools and browse the full catalog through them — for clients with hard tool caps and no tool search of their own (Cursor, Windsurf).
environmentVariables.name: IONOS_MCP_LOAD_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Opt in to write operations. Unset (default) leaves the server read-only: only list_/get_/head_ tools are registered. 'write' additionally registers create_/update_ tools and the non-disruptive actions (start_, resume_, attach_, assign_); 'destructive' also registers delete_ and the disruptive actions (stop_, reboot_, suspend_, upgrade_, restore_, detach_, recreate_, import_) and implies 'write'. Comma-separated, case-insensitive, hierarchical; unrecognised values stay read-only. WARNING: enabling this lets an AI model provision, modify and delete billable resources in a live IONOS CLOUD account. Every create and delete requires a two-phase confirmation, but that cannot stop a client configured to approve tool calls automatically. Leave unset unless writes are needed.
environmentVariables.name: IONOS_MCP_TOOL_SCOPE

capabilities: Play, pause, skip and queue tracks in the Music app
Search your library and the Apple Music catalog
Create playlists and add tracks, including tracks you do not own yet
Read and set ratings, and browse recently played
Export your library and take snapshots of it

distribution.note: The primary channel is a notarized macOS app: download, drag to Applications, double-click. The first-run window installs the background helper and writes the MCP client config. The PyPI package in `packages` is the same server for people who prefer a terminal install; it bundles the same signed MusicKit helper, so it is not a reduced build.

privacy.credentials: None stored. Apple's MusicKit signs each request from the app's own code-signing identity plus a one-time consent prompt.
privacy.network: Apple's public catalog endpoints and Apple Music's own API. No third-party service, no telemetry.
privacy.permissions: Automation access to the Music app, and Apple Music access. No Accessibility, no browser automation, no synthetic clicks.

requirements.account: No Apple Developer account, no API key, and no token are required.
requirements.arch: Apple Silicon or Intel (both are published)
requirements.needs: The Music app, signed into Apple Music. A subscription is required for catalog playback and adds.

io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.authentication: One complete MCP product case is free. Start market_access_check with a plain-language message and no case_id. Then follow the returned state and next_action, carrying the opaque case_id unchanged. Answer clarification questions by their stable keys. Stage 2 runs after seller confirmation or an active case-scoped delegation. Browser actions declare delegated_execution: an agent with the listed authority and required capability may complete them; otherwise give the URL to the seller. Payment needs a separate mandate covering the displayed amount, currency and terms. Never infer permission. A new product or SKU requires paid API access. describe_coverage and watch_product_regulatory_changes stay open.
io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.safetyBoundary: Market-access readiness only. Not legal advice, certification, product approval, or marketplace approval guarantee.

environmentVariables.description: BigQuery: path to a service-account key file (Application Default Credentials). Required to use the bigquery engine.
environmentVariables.name: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: account identifier. Required to use the snowflake engine.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: username. Required to use the snowflake engine.
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_USER

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: role to assume. Required to use the snowflake engine; has no default and must never be ACCOUNTADMIN (ACCOUNTADMIN, SECURITYADMIN and ORGADMIN are rejected before any Snowflake connection is opened - the check runs when the Snowflake configuration is first loaded, on the first Snowflake tool call; the server process itself starts regardless, so a bad role surfaces as a failed check_credentials or a tool error, not as a startup exit).
environmentVariables.name: SNOWFLAKE_ROLE

environmentVariables.description: Snowflake: secondary roles activated at login. NONE (default) means only SNOWFLAKE_ROLE is active in the session; ALL is the explicit opt-out that activates every role granted to SNOWFLAKE_USER.

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 to let estimate_query_cost/run_query_bounded accept text containing more than one SQL statement. Off by default: the cost cap is only known to cover the single statement the dry run/EXPLAIN priced. Skips only this server's scanner: Snowflake still rejects multi-statement text (sessions are pinned to MULTI_STATEMENT_COUNT=1), and only a single SELECT/WITH/VALUES statement is wrapped in a LIMIT subquery - a script runs unwrapped and its row cap (max_rows, default 1000) is enforced by the paged fetch.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_ALLOW_MULTI_STATEMENT_SQL

environmentVariables.description: Set to 1 (exactly that value) to let estimate_query_cost/run_query_bounded accept statements that are not reads. Off by default: only text whose first keyword (after comments and opening parentheses) is SELECT, WITH, VALUES, SHOW, DESCRIBE, DESC or EXPLAIN is estimated or run - a WITH must be followed by a SELECT or VALUES - because warehouse rows re-enter the model's context and can steer the next call. The gate is defence in depth: the authorisation boundary is the credential's grants (deploy a read-only principal). With COST_GUARD_ALLOW_MULTI_STATEMENT_SQL=1 every statement in the text must be a read, so BigQuery scripts (DECLARE/SET/BEGIN) need both opt-outs. Any other value leaves the gate on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_ALLOW_WRITE_STATEMENTS

environmentVariables.description: Maximum number of run_query_bounded calls allowed in flight at once (positive integer, default 8). A cancelled call keeps its slot until its warehouse query completes or the 120 s watchdog fires; a call over the cap fails with a tool error naming this variable before any warehouse connection is opened.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_MAX_IN_FLIGHT_QUERIES

environmentVariables.description: Set to true (exactly that value) to let the read-only Databricks tools (check_credentials, estimate_query_cost) open a session on a SQL warehouse that is not RUNNING, which starts the warehouse and bills compute until it auto-stops. Off by default: the server first reads the warehouse's state through the Warehouses API (GET /api/2.0/sql/warehouses/<id>, CAN_VIEW/CAN_USE suffices) and, unless it is RUNNING - also when the state cannot be read - check_credentials returns ok=false and estimate_query_cost returns no byte or dollar figure, without opening a session. run_query_bounded is not gated: its own pre-execution estimate and the execution may start the warehouse. Any other value leaves the guard on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_DATABRICKS_ALLOW_WAREHOUSE_START

environmentVariables.description: Set to true (exactly that value) to let the read-only Snowflake tools run SELECT CURRENT_REGION(), the INFORMATION_SCHEMA.QUERY_HISTORY read and check_credentials' session-context SELECT on a warehouse that is not STARTED, which can resume a suspended AUTO_RESUME warehouse and bill compute until it auto-suspends. Off by default: those statements are skipped unless the pinned warehouse's SHOW WAREHOUSES state is STARTED (also skipped when no warehouse is pinned or the state cannot be read), and the QUERY_HISTORY read is skipped whenever estimate_query_cost is called without a warehouse argument; estimate_query_cost then prices at Gen1 rates with the byte-tier heuristic and says so in a caveat, and check_credentials returns ok=true with a detail built from the SHOW WAREHOUSES row. USE WAREHOUSE, EXPLAIN USING JSON, SHOW WAREHOUSES and SELECT CURRENT_WAREHOUSE() always run; run_query_bounded is not gated. Any other value leaves the guard on.
environmentVariables.name: COST_GUARD_SNOWFLAKE_ALLOW_WAREHOUSE_RESUME

environmentVariables.description: Register apple_safari_network_record, _list and _get, which record what a page you allowed the extension on fetches and read the responses. Its own gate rather than allowWrites, because it is a read; off means the tools do not exist. Headers named like credentials are masked, bodies are not. Reloading a tab to record and saving a body to a file still need APPLE_SAFARI_ALLOW_WRITES.

environmentVariables.description: Register apple_safari_cookies, which lists the cookies Safari would send to an open page, HttpOnly ones included, through the extension's cookies permission. Its own gate rather than allowWrites, because it is a read; off means the tool does not exist. Not enough on its own: only sites in APPLE_SAFARI_COOKIE_HOSTS are readable. Values never come back inline; saveAs writes named ones to a 0600 file and needs APPLE_SAFARI_ALLOW_WRITES.
environmentVariables.name: APPLE_SAFARI_ALLOW_COOKIES

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated registrable domains whose cookies apple_safari_cookies may read, like "yahoo.com"; each covers the domain and its subdomains. Empty, the default, means no site is readable. An entry with no dot is ignored.

environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_PYTHON_BACKEND

environmentVariables.description: Encryption suite to negotiate for the secure channel. Anything other than None needs a client certificate and key. The two AES suites are Node-only: the Python runtime refuses them at startup rather than downgrading. None is unencrypted and unauthenticated, and keeps control tools blocked unless insecure control is explicitly allowed. An unknown policy stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_SECURITY_POLICY

environmentVariables.description: Message security mode for the secure channel. Sign authenticates messages without encrypting them. A policy with mode None, or a mode without a policy, stops the server at startup; leaving it blank never downgrades a policy to signing only. Leave blank for SignAndEncrypt once a security policy is set, otherwise None.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_SECURITY_MODE

environmentVariables.description: Path to the certificate (PEM or DER) this client presents as its application identity. Required by any security policy other than None. A path that does not exist stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_CLIENT_CERT

environmentVariables.description: Path to the private key matching the client certificate. A path, never key material. Whoever can read the file can impersonate this client: keep it readable only by the account running the server. A path that does not exist stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_CLIENT_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Application URI announced to the server. Set it only for a certificate that carries no URI of its own. A configured URI that conflicts with the certificate is refused before connecting. Leave blank for the subjectAltName URI of the client certificate.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_APPLICATION_URI

environmentVariables.description: Path to the OPC UA server's own certificate (PEM or DER), pinned: a server presenting any other certificate cannot complete the handshake. Control tools (writes, method calls, alarm actions) require it, or OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE instead. Requires a security policy other than None. Unset, encryption protects against eavesdropping but not against an impostor endpoint, so control tools are refused unless OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE validates the server or OPCUA_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_SERVER_CONTROL is set. Set without a security policy, it stops the server at startup rather than pinning nothing; a pinned certificate that has expired or is not yet valid refuses to connect.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_SERVER_CERT

environmentVariables.description: Directory with trusted/certs root CAs, issuers/certs intermediate CAs, and trusted/crl plus issuers/crl signed current revocation lists. Authenticate the OPC UA peer by its validated chain and expected server URI. Requires secured channel and OPCUA_SERVER_APPLICATION_URI; Python requires the maintained asyncua backend. Missing, stale, forged or revoked trust material refuses connection. Cannot be combined with an exact server certificate pin.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE

environmentVariables.description: ApplicationUri of the intended OPC UA server. Must match the peer certificate URI SAN and advertised application identity. Required with OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_SERVER_APPLICATION_URI

environmentVariables.description: OPC UA username. The session is anonymous when unset. Cannot be combined with a user certificate. Requires a password; either one alone stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_USERNAME

environmentVariables.description: Password for the username. Without a security policy it crosses the network in clear text. Supply it through the client's secret storage, never on a command line.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_PASSWORD

environmentVariables.description: Path to the certificate identifying the user, for X.509 user authentication: a different key pair from the client certificate, which secures the channel. Requires the user key and a security policy other than None; cannot be combined with a username. Any of those combinations broken stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_USER_CERT

environmentVariables.description: Path to the private key for the user certificate. It signs the server's challenge and is never sent. Whoever can read the file can log in as this user: keep it readable only by the account running the server.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_USER_KEY

environmentVariables.description: Which tools are offered. observe reads, browses, reads history and monitors; operator adds explicitly allowlisted writes, method calls and alarm actions; full exposes every tool and is meant only for a tightly scoped OPC UA account. Unset fails closed to observe; an unknown profile stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_PROFILE

environmentVariables.description: Path to a version-1 JSON policy file, the only place per-node value bounds, writable_subtrees, preconditions, the alarm scope and deny_read can be set. Every policy variable that is set overrides what the file says. An unreadable or invalid file stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_POLICY_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated tool allowlist. It can only narrow the selected profile, never widen it. An unknown tool name stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_ALLOWED_TOOLS

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated exact node IDs the operator profile may write, as ns=2;i=5 or, stable across a server restart, nsu=<namespace-uri>;i=5 or a browse path from the Root folder such as /Objects/Line1/Setpoint. Setting it replaces the policy file's list, bounds included. Empty fails closed: operator can write nothing. A batch write with any target outside the list is refused before it reaches OPC UA.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_ALLOWED_WRITE_NODES

environmentVariables.description: Comma-separated object_node_id|method_node_id pairs the operator profile may call. Either half may be a browse path from the Root folder. Empty fails closed: operator can call nothing. An entry without | stops the server at startup.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_ALLOWED_METHODS

environmentVariables.description: Let the operator profile act on alarms: acknowledge_alarm and every act_on_alarm action.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_ALLOW_ACKNOWLEDGE_ALARMS

environmentVariables.description: Permit control tools on an OPC UA channel with no security policy (None). Does not cover a secured channel to an unverified server; that is OPCUA_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_SERVER_CONTROL. Fail-open override: writes, method calls and alarm actions then travel unauthenticated and unencrypted. Reported as control=INSECURE-OVERRIDE in the startup line, get_server_status and every audit record. Never enable it against production equipment.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_ALLOW_INSECURE_CONTROL

environmentVariables.description: Permit control tools on a secured OPC UA channel whose server is not authenticated: neither pinned with OPCUA_SERVER_CERT nor validated by OPCUA_SERVER_TRUST_STORE. Does not cover a channel with no security policy; that is OPCUA_ALLOW_INSECURE_CONTROL. Fail-open override: writes, method calls and alarm actions are then encrypted to whichever server answered the endpoint, which may be an impostor. Reported as control=UNVERIFIED-OVERRIDE in the startup line, get_server_status and every audit record. Never enable it against production equipment.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_SERVER_CONTROL

environmentVariables.description: Allow a write outside the EURange the OPC UA server itself published for the node. A published InstrumentRange still applies. Fail-open override: it discards the only value bound a deployment with no policy file has.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_ALLOW_OUT_OF_RANGE_WRITES

environmentVariables.description: Path to an append-only file for the control audit trail, one JSON object per line, written beside stderr. Created owner-only (0600) if it does not exist; reopened when rotated away. A file that cannot be opened, or that is a symlink, not a regular file, another account's, or group/world-writable, stops the server rather than falling back to stderr alone. While set, a control call whose record cannot be written is refused (fail closed); reads continue.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_AUDIT_FILE

environmentVariables.description: When an audit-file record counts as written. always fsyncs each record before the control call proceeds, so it survives a power loss; none leaves it to the operating system, so it survives only a crash of this process. none can lose the records of control calls that already reached the plant if the machine loses power.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_AUDIT_FSYNC

environmentVariables.description: Adds seq, prev_hash and hash to every audit record so edits, deletions and reordering can be detected with --verify-audit. sha256 catches accidental or naive edits; hmac-sha256 also resists anyone without the key. Requires the audit file. Set without an audit file, or hmac-sha256 without a key file, stops the server. No chain detects a truncated tail.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_AUDIT_CHAIN

environmentVariables.description: Path to the HMAC key for the hmac-sha256 audit chain: at least 32 bytes, for example from openssl rand -hex 32. Surrounding whitespace is ignored. Whoever can read the key can forge the chain: a key readable or writable by group or others stops the server. Refused unless the chain is hmac-sha256.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_AUDIT_CHAIN_KEY_FILE

environmentVariables.description: Label stamped on every audit record as operator_label, so a shipped log says which deployment a control call came from. Configured, never verified: it is not an identity, and mcp_principal stays null.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_OPERATOR_ID

environmentVariables.description: Wait before the first attempt to repair a dropped or refused connection, in milliseconds. It doubles with each further attempt.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_RECONNECT_INITIAL_DELAY_MS

environmentVariables.description: Ceiling for the doubling retry delay, in milliseconds.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_RECONNECT_MAX_DELAY_MS

environmentVariables.description: Retries after the first attempt, per connection round, before a tool call gives up: a whole number from -1 to 1000. 0 never retries; -1 never stops trying, in bounded rounds of four retries so no single call waits forever.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_RECONNECT_MAX_RETRY

environmentVariables.description: Session lifetime asked of the OPC UA server, in milliseconds. It also sets the keep-alive period, so it decides how quickly an idle connection notices the server has gone.
environmentVariables.name: OPCUA_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Milliseconds a MongoDB connection may stay unused (no tool call touching it) before it is closed to release the underlying connection pool and its server-side state. Applied per connection regardless of its connection scope; the preconfigured connection is excluded, and the reaper runs on this cadence. Set to 0 to disable reaping; must not be negative.
environmentVariables.name: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS

environmentVariables.description: Visibility scope for MongoDB connections created at runtime. With 'session' (the default), each MCP session only sees the connections it created (plus the shared 'preconfigured' one) and they are closed when the session ends. With 'global', connections are shared across all sessions and survive session rotation. Deprecated: the MCP protocol is moving to sessionless, so this option will soon be removed and the connection scope will default to 'global'. For shared-server use cases, use the Atlas-Managed MCP server or build an authenticated library using the @mongodb-js/mcp-cli package. Note: on the sessionless (2026-07-28) HTTP path, a request without an mcp-session-id falls back to the shared ('global') scope so it can still persist connections across requests; the legacy sessionful path always carries a server-issued session.
environmentVariables.name: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_SCOPE

environmentVariables.description: MongoDB connection string for direct database connections, exposed under the connectionId "preconfigured". Optional, if not set, you'll need to call the connect tool before interacting with MongoDB data. Deprecated: prefer the "preconfigured" entry of connectionStrings.
environmentVariables.name: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING

environmentVariables.description: MongoDB connection strings keyed by name, as a JSON object (e.g. {"preconfigured": "mongodb://...", "analytics": "mongodb://..."}). Each name becomes a connectionId that the MongoDB tools can use directly, so one server can reach several deployments. Connections are opened on first use. Environment variable or config file only.
environmentVariables.name: MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRINGS

environmentVariables.description: When set to true, allows binding the HTTP server (and monitoring server) to a non-loopback host such as 0.0.0.0, a LAN IP, or an empty host (all interfaces). Binding to a non-loopback host exposes the server to the entire network and can allow unauthorized access. Off by default: the server refuses to start on a non-loopback host unless this is true.
